basic_identification.full_title: Indian Standard Identification Colours for Schemes for Ships' Ventilation Systems
basic_identification.sector_category: Marine Engineering and Shipbuilding (approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Shipbuilding Sectional Committee under the Indian Standards Institution)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the identification colours for functional plans of ventilation systems on board ships. It is intended to be applied only when identification of such systems by color is deemed necessary to ensure clear communication and structural safety.

version_status_and_amendments.edition_year_of_copy: First Edition, February 1980 (Reaffirmed in 2002, Reviewed and Reaffirmed in 2023)
version_status_and_amendments.supersedes: None (developed as a new specialized national marine drafting and outfitting color protocol)

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Procedural Specification / Identification Code (Marine Drafting / Shipbuilding)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Engineering Practice and Drafting Standard. Since IS 9423:1980 is a procedural code of practice for design office schematics rather than a safety-critical consumer product, it is certified on a voluntary basis. However, compliance with this standard is universally mandated inside all Indian Navy, Coast Guard, public shipyards (e.g., MDL, GRSE, GSL), commercial shipbuilders, and maritime classification societies (such as IRS and Lloyd's Register) during the approval of functional ventilation, HVAC, and outfitting drawings.

requirements.detail: Specifies identification colours for functional plans to be used for ventilation systems on board ships, only when identification by colour is necessary to ensure safety and system clarity.
Explicitly notes that the colour references given in Table 1 are for guidance only, allowing minor variations in paint shades as long as system distinctions remain unambiguous.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 9423 : 1980 (Reaffirmed 2023) is the national Indian Standard specifying the standardized color-coding schemes to be used on shipboard functional drawings and ventilation plans. Finalized under the Shipbuilding Sectional Committee, it coordinates with the paint standards of IS 5:1978 to assign unique, recognizable colors and shade numbers to 8 distinct ventilation circuits. These range from Yellow (Shade 309) for natural supply air and Green (Shade 218) for mechanical atmospheric air, to Dark Blue (Shade 166) for refrigerated air, Violet (Shade 796) for conditioned air, and Grey (Shade 694) for mechanical exhaust systems. This uniform drafting framework ensures that shipyard outfitting teams, ship crew members, and marine safety inspectors can instantly identify and trace various air flows on shipboard schematics.
